seytansofrasi.name: Şeytan Sofrası
seytansofrasi.slogan: The devil's table is set with islands and a sinking sun.
seytansofrasi.line: The hill, whose name means Satan's Dinner Table, gives a panorama of the Ayvalık islands, best at sunset.

kyzikos.name: Kyzikos
kyzikos.slogan: A lost city of marble, tied to the mainland by a sandbar.
kyzikos.line: Its Temple of Hadrian had 21-metre columns, the tallest known in the ancient world.

taksiyarhisayvalik.name: Taksiyarhis Church
taksiyarhisayvalik.slogan: An archangels' church that outlived the town's Greek centuries.
taksiyarhisayvalik.line: Ayvalık's Greek population was exchanged for Muslims from Greece under the 1923 agreement.

laleadasi.name: Lale Adası
laleadasi.slogan: Walk out over the water to an island of sea and sunsets.
laleadasi.line: Cunda, the largest of the Ayvalık Islands, was called Moschonisia by the Greeks and is linked to the mainland by a causeway built in the late 1960s.

antandros.name: Antandros
antandros.slogan: Ida's timber made this hillside harbour a shipyard of empires.
antandros.line: In Virgil's Aeneid, Aeneas builds his fleet here below Mount Ida before sailing away from fallen Troy.
